PURPOSE. The page computes Briggsian logarithms of Gauss's factorial function Π(z)=Γ(z+1) at z = 9.0, 9.2, …, 10.8 and checks them. These values are the end-points for the table on the next page, which gives log Π(z) for z = 9.20 … 10.20 in steps of 0.02, with three orders of differences. The only transcendental inputs are x = Π(0.2) = Γ(1.2) and y = Π(0.4) = Γ(1.4). The page then checks x and y through Gauss's summation formula for F(α,β,γ,1).

(1) Reflection step. Gauss uses Π(z)Π(−z) = πz/sin(πz) together with Π(z) = zΠ(z−1):
- Π(0.6) = 0.6·Π(−0.4) = 0.6·0.4π/(y sin72°) = 0.24π/(y sin72°).
- Π(0.8) = 0.8·Π(−0.2) = 0.16π/(x sin36°).

(2) Exact rational factors. Each product of the form 1.r·2.r·…·9.r is written in factored form:
- Π9 = 9! = 10·189·192 = 362880, so log = 5.5597630329.
- Π9.2 = x·(12·22·…·92)/10^9 = x·621345.5…, so log = 5.7933324049 + log x. The written factorization 1066·1023·966·768 lacks one factor 768. The true product is 2^18·3^4·7·11·13·23·31·41 = 1066·1023·966·768².
- Π9.4 = y·(14·24·…·94)/10^9 = y·192³·329·561·777/10^9, so log = 6.0064834641 + log y.
- Π9.6 = Π0.6·(1.6·…·9.6) = π·96⁴·462·988·989/(10^11·y·sin72°), so log = 6.1026236910 − log y.
- Π9.8 = π·672³·528·493·494/(10^11·x·sin36°), so log = 6.3192467973 − log x.
- Π10 = 10! = 100·189·192, so log = 6.5597630329.
- Π(10+r) = (10+r)·Π(9+r). Adding log 10.2 etc. gives the second block: 6.8019325766 + log x; 7.0235168034 + log y; 7.1279295563 − log y; 7.3526705528 − log x.
- Check against known factorials: log 12! = 8.6803369640, minus log 12 = 1.0791812460, gives log 11! = 7.6011557180. log 11 = 1.0413926852 gives back log 10!.

(3) Values of x and y. log x = log Γ(1.2) = 9.9629225048 (i.e. −0.0370774952) and log y = 9.9480527735 are inserted. This gives the third column, log Π(9.2), …, log Π(10.8):
5.7562549097, 5.9545362376, 6.1545709175, 6.3563242925, 6.5597630329, 6.7648550815, 6.9715695769, 7.1798767828, 7.3897480480.

(4) Differences (units 10^-10).
- First differences: 19649.18768, 19828.13279, 20003.46799, 20175.33750, 20343.87404, 20509.20486, 20671.44954, 20830.72059, 20987.12652.
- Second differences: 178.94511, 175.33520, 171.86951, 168.53654, 165.33082, 162.24468, 159.27105, 156.40593.
- Extrapolation [my reading of the isolated numbers]: the next second difference is extrapolated as 153.64048. That gives a first difference of 21140.76700, and 7.3897480480 + 0.2114076700 = 7.6011557180 = log 11!. This closing check succeeds.

(5) Check by Gauss's summation formula. Gauss uses F(α,β,γ,1) = Π(γ−1)Π(γ−α−β−1)/(Π(γ−α−1)Π(γ−β−1)). Each log F therefore equals a second difference of the table:
- F(−1/5,−1/5,10,1) = Π9·Π9.4/Π9.2². Series value 1.0041288636, log = 0.0017894511 = 178.94511. This agrees.
- F(−1/5,−1/5,10⅕,1) = Π9.2·Π9.6/Π9.4². Series value 1.0040454154, whose log is actually 0.0017533574; the table gives 175.33520. These differ by about 5.4·10^-10 in the log.
- The difference in log y − 2 log x and in log x − 3 log y fixes the two unknowns. Solving gives δlog x ≈ −1.1e-10 and δlog y ≈ −2.1e-10. These are exactly the corrections visible on the next page: 9.20 → …49087, 9.40 → …62355, 9.60 → …09196, 9.80 → …42935, 10.20 → …50805, versus 49097, 62376, 09175, 42925, 50815 here.

(6) Two hypergeometric series summed term by term.
- F(1/5,1/5,11,1) = 1 + 1·1/(5·55) + 1·1·6·6/(5·10·55·60) + …, using the term ratio (α+n)(β+n)/((n+1)(γ+n)). Sum = 1.0038882486.7, including a tail estimate of 0.7. It should equal Π10·Π9.6/Π9.8².
- F(−1/5,1/5,11,1) = 1 − 0.0037996447.5 = 0.9962003552.5. It should equal Π10²/(Π10.2·Π9.8). The correct log is 9.9983466923.

(7) Analytic part (natural logs).
- Λz = log k! + z log k − Σ_{i=1..k} log(z+i), i.e. Gauss's finite Π(k,z), which tends to log Π(z) as k→∞.
- Λ'z = log k − Σ1/(z+i) (the digamma ψ(z+1), Gauss's Ψ).
- Λ''z = Σ1/(z+i)², Λ'''z = −2Σ1/(z+i)³.
- Taylor expansion: Λ(z+ω) = Λz + ω(1+1/2+…+1/z − 0.5772…) + ½ω²Σ1/(z+i)² − ⅓ω³Σ1/(z+i)³ + ¼ω⁴Σ1/(z+i)⁴ − …. The constant is written only as '−0,' and left unfinished [completion as Euler's constant is mine]. This is the tool for interpolating at steps of 0.02.
errors: The rational factor of Π9.2 is written 1066·1023·966·768 : 10^9, but the product 12·22·…·92 needs 768² (the logarithm 5.79333 24048.81 uses the correct product). This is a notational slip, or a superscript the transcription missed.

Series for F(1/5,1/5,11,1): the 7th term should be 3280.1·(6.2²)/(7·17) = 1059.6, not 1130.5. All later terms inherit the factor 1130.5/1059.6. The correct sum is ≈1.0038882372, not 1.0038882487, and its log 0.0016853654 then agrees exactly with the table.

Series for F(−1/5,1/5,11,1): the 7th term should be 1307.4·(5.8·6.2)/(7·17) = 395.1, not 388.5. Correcting it (+≈10 units) and using the right log (9.9983466923; the transcription reads 66983) reproduces the table value −0.0016533082.

The log of 1.0040454154 is 0.0017533574, not the 0.0017533520 written beside it (that number is the table's second difference). The 5.4e-10 discrepancy is what drives the small corrections to log x and log y adopted on the next page.
The Taylor formula for Λ(z+ω) leaves the constant unfinished ('−0,'); ψ(z+1) = H_z − γ for integer z.
The pre-correction values on this page (e.g. log Π9.2 = 5.7562549097) are off by 1–2 units of 1e-10; Gauss himself superseded them on the next page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is computational working material for Gauss's well-known log Π table and the hypergeometric summation formula of his 1812 memoir. The only interest is in the archival detail of how he checked Γ(1.2) and Γ(1.4).

checkable.asserts: coefficients ψ(z+1), ψ1/2, ψ2/6, ψ3/24 = ±(1/n)Σ1/(z+i)^n, as in Λ(z+ω)
